transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-07-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Recording ID: frfly-20260707-knotwell-0a9b

Summary (auto): quick alignment on legal timeline and pilot plan; security questions noted; pricing pathway and SLA negotiation discussed.

00:00 Maya Torres (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'm Maya with Redwood Inference, joining with Liam our solutions engineer and Renee from customer success. nice to meet you all.
00:12 Aisha Khan (Head of AI): thanks Maya, appreciate you fitting us in. we wanted to get through our legal checklist and the pilot plan so we can get procurement running.
00:23 Tom Reeves (Procurement): morning. quick ask up front — what's your standard timeline for returning an MSA with DPA changes? our buying window is tight.
00:32 Maya Torres (AE): totally understood. on average we aim to turn MSA/DPA redlines in 3 business days for standard asks, more complex carve-outs can take longer. we'll propose a path: redline by us by Friday, you give feedback by the 21st ideally.
00:47 Sara Nguyen (Security Manager): thanks. also need clarity on SOC 2 scope and whether you offer customer-managed KMS or bring-your-own-key for the private deployment.
00:55 Liam Zhang (SE): yes for private we support customer KMS via HSM integrations; for hosted we have envelope encryption and can integrate with customer-managed keys in supported regions — we can share the KMS integration doc.
01:12 Diego Marquez (Cloud Architect): and what about VPC connectivity? we need predictable egress IPs for firewall rules.
01:20 Liam Zhang (SE): for dedicated and private deployments we provide static egress IP ranges and can set up VPC peering — we'll include the IP block list in the connectivity guide. for hosted, we have regional endpoints but egress is less predictable unless you buy dedicated capacity.
01:38 Tom Reeves (Procurement): SLA — what's your uptime SLA for hosted vs dedicated, and do you have credits for latency misses? procurement is going to ask.
01:46 Maya Torres (AE): our standard hosted SLA is 99.5% availability; dedicated customers can get 99.9%+, and we offer service credits for major outages. latency SLOs are defined per model/profile in the performance sheet; credits for latency regressions are discussed in enterprise agreements.
02:05 Aisha Khan (Head of AI): we care more about P50/P95 latency for our inference surface. can the pilot measure both latency and cost per 1k tokens so our FinOps can sign off?
02:16 Liam Zhang (SE): absolutely — pilot will run with telemetry for p50/p95 p99, token counts, and cost modeling. we'll export CSV and a short dashboard.
02:27 Maya Torres (AE): we'll attach a pilot benchmark template. Liam — propose a small sample workload to mirror Aisha's production traces.
02:34 Liam Zhang (SE): noted. Diego, can you share a few representative traces after the call? even anonymized.
02:40 Diego Marquez (Cloud Architect): yes i can share. i'll scrub prod ids.
02:44 Sara Nguyen (Security Manager): on data handling — does Redwood retain prompts or outputs by default? what are retention configs?
02:51 Maya Torres (AE): by default hosted logs are retained 30 days for troubleshooting; customers can opt out, and for dedicated/private we support custom retention policies and log forwarding to customer's SIEM. DPA will codify retention.
03:03 Tom Reeves (Procurement): pricing approvals — we need a clear sheet that maps committed throughput to unit pricing and what the step-downs to hosted are.
03:12 Maya Torres (AE): we'll send the pricing-sheet.xlsx that shows tiered pricing, committed monthly GPUs for dedicated, and burst pricing. also call out data egress fees if you enable KMS-managed egress in certain regions.
03:26 Aisha Khan (Head of AI): question on model variants — if we pick a quantized variant for cost reasons, how do you guarantee semantic parity? we can't introduce hallucination regressions.
03:38 Liam Zhang (SE): good point. we run eval suites during model onboarding; for pilot we'll run your evals and produce rouge/accuracy/intent metrics. if a quantized/optimized variant regresses beyond a threshold, we won't push it to production for the rollout.
03:55 Sara Nguyen (Security Manager): can we get encryption at rest verified in your SOC2? do you have penetration test reports?
04:02 Renee Park (CSM): yes we have a SOC2 Type II report and pen test summary; we'll share the artifacts under NDA.
04:09 Tom Reeves (Procurement): about contract language — Knotwell has a standard clause matrix especially around liability caps and data residency. some of our customers require a 100% residency guarantee, how do you manage that?
04:22 Maya Torres (AE): for strict residency we recommend the private deployment in your cloud region or our private offering on-prem. that gives you full control over residency and keys. For hosted we can commit to region-based processing but cannot 100% guarantee if cross-region failover is necessary — that's usually captured as an exception.
04:43 Diego Marquez (Cloud Architect): for the pilot we prefer dedicated capacity in our region to avoid noisy neighbor issues. what's the lead time?
04:50 Maya Torres (AE): reserved dedicated pools can be provisioned in 2-3 weeks depending on capacity; for an initial 48-hour pilot we can carve a short-lived dedicated lane or run in a burst mode if capacity allows. we'll identify the fastest path after legal ok.
05:07 Aisha Khan (Head of AI): on latency sensitivity — our product surfaces chat for financial advisors. p95 needs to be < 350ms for a 1k token request. is that feasible?
05:17 Liam Zhang (SE): with dedicated and the right batching settings it's feasible. depends on model choice and quantization. We'll simulate with your traces.
05:26 Tom Reeves (Procurement): any references for SOC2 and contract examples with other finance customers? we need peer validation.
05:34 Maya Torres (AE): we can share redacted references and a one-pager of finance customers; we'll include the SOC2 package and a sanitized case study.
05:42 Sara Nguyen (Security Manager): final point — access controls, RBAC, SSO. we use SAML 2.0 with SCIM for onboarding.
05:50 Liam Zhang (SE): supported — SAML/SCIM provisioning, role mapping in Console, and audit logs. we'll attach the SSO integration guide.
06:00 Maya Torres (AE): ok let's recap next steps. we'll send an updated MSA/DPA with the requested retention and KMS language by Friday. Liam will circulate the pilot plan. Diego will provide anonymized traces. Tom will push to legal and share your clause matrix.
06:15 Tom Reeves (Procurement): understood. target for our internal legal to respond by July 21. If redlines are small we can sign earlier.
06:22 Aisha Khan (Head of AI): and we'll aim to have the pilot window week of July 20, pending sign-off.
06:30 Renee Park (CSM): i'll open the pilot workspace and pre-provision credentials upon legal clearance; that'll help speed ramp.
06:40 Maya Torres (AE): great. i will follow up with email that includes links: security-deck.pdf, pricing-sheet.xlsx, msadpa-proposed-redline.pdf and the pilot-template.csv.
06:52 Diego Marquez (Cloud Architect): one more thing — are there any known cost exposure items we should watch during the pilot? e.g., egress fees, large KV cache persistence?
07:00 Liam Zhang (SE): egress is the biggest. also long context windows increase token cost, and continuous KV caching for many concurrent sessions can raise memory-backed billing for dedicated setups. we'll annotate the pilot plan with expected cost levers.
07:15 Tom Reeves (Procurement): ok that's helpful. 
07:20 Maya Torres (AE): thanks everyone. we'll circulate notes and next steps.

Meeting Close: 15:55 UTC

References shared: pricing-sheet.xlsx, security-deck.pdf, pilot-template.csv, msadpa-proposed-redline.pdf
